learningObjectives: Know how and when to use Conditions.

elements.text: Conditional instantiation controls which model elements are generated for each data combination. It is different from evaluating an IF or WHILE against the live SUT at execution. Supported conditional targets include the Template, TemplateInstance, TestStep folders, TestSteps/XTestSteps and XTestStepValues. Use the narrowest intended scope. Later condition edits require regeneration of existing cases.

Add Condition through Column Chooser or edit the property. Link the Template to its data source first. Dragging an ordinary Instance into a Condition creates an equality comparison; inspect the generated expression. Attribute conditions default to a non-null check, with special handling for NULL and EMPTY Instances. Use == for equality and != for inequality; && combines required clauses and || accepts either clause. Do not rely on an assumed default OR. Quoted strings and valid source paths matter. A != exclusion also accepts other unexpected values, so use it only when the intended domain makes that safe. Numeric comparison should use the documented numeric syntax or conversion. Dotted icon outlines indicate condition-based instantiation.

Run Check Template, inspect the selected instance source and manual changes, then regenerate. Inspect which cases and steps were actually generated and trial-run meaningful valid/negative paths. Generation and schema checking alone do not certify a complete working test set.

Independent practice: synthetic payment data includes a controlled non-null domain of Visa, MasterCard and No Credit Card used. Compare a deliberate exclusion with an explicit allowed-value condition, inspect generated subsets and their assertions. Original Academy payment exercise material was inaccessible and remains unverified.

examPitfalls.title: Generation and execution conditions differ
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting a generation condition to inspect live runtime state.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use conditional instantiation for model/data selection and runtime IF/loops for runtime branching.

examPitfalls.title: Exclusion is broader than an allowlist
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using != as a universal substitute for listing allowed values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the complete domain, including missing or unexpected values.

examPitfalls.title: Scope changes generated structure
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Gating a whole folder when only one value should vary.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the intended object scope and inspect generated steps.

examPitfalls.title: Validation does not certify execution
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Declaring the generated set working before assertions run.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Validate the model, regenerate and trial-run the intended outcomes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which listed group contains supported scopes within a Template for conditional instantiation (not an exhaustive list)?

options.text: TestStepFolder, TestStep and XTestStepValue.
ExecutionList, RequirementSet, and TestSheet level.
Attribute, Instance, and Module level.
Only at the TestCase level.

practiceQuiz.hint: These are the three levels of granularity inside a Template.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These are supported targets; the Template and TemplateInstance are also supported. These conditions choose generated elements, not runtime IF branches.

optionExplanations.A: These are supported internal scopes, though other targets are also supported.
optionExplanations.B: These are not the listed internal Template scopes for conditional instantiation.
optionExplanations.C: Module scanning and source design objects are not this set of Template targets.
optionExplanations.D: The mechanism is not limited to the TestCase itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A controlled, non-null payment domain contains only Visa, MasterCard and No Credit Card used. Which compact condition includes the two card choices during generation?

options.text: A chain of OR conditions, one per specific credit card brand.
No condition is needed; all TestSteps always run.
'Payment Method.Credit Card' == "Visa" OR == "MasterCard" OR == "Amex" (and so on for every card).
'Payment Method.Credit Card' != "No Credit Card used"

practiceQuiz.hint: A single != is simpler and more business-readable than many ORs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Within this explicitly limited domain, excluding the sentinel selects the two intended card choices. Outside that domain, != can include unintended values.

optionExplanations.A: A brand-by-brand enumeration is unnecessary for the controlled domain stated.
optionExplanations.B: Without a condition the sentinel combination is not excluded here.
optionExplanations.C: This incomplete OR text is not the single compact exclusion requested.
optionExplanations.D: Excluding the sentinel selects the two card values in this explicitly limited domain.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the explicit logical operator || mean in a conditional-instantiation expression?

options.text: NOT — none of the conditions may be true.
AND — all conditions must be true.
OR — only one of the conditions needs to be true.
XOR — exactly one condition must be true, no more.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the more permissive of the two common logical operators.
practiceQuiz.rationale: OR accepts either clause; it is not a claim that Tosca always inserts OR when multiple conditions are added.

optionExplanations.A: NOT negates a clause rather than accepting either.
optionExplanations.B: AND requires both clauses, unlike the operator asked about.
optionExplanations.C: OR accepts either clause, including the case where both hold.
optionExplanations.D: XOR requires exactly one true clause and is not the meaning of ||.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must be visible in the Template grid before you can set a Condition, and how do you add it?

options.text: The XL Reference column, enabled from the Property tab.
The RequirementSet column — enable it via Execution settings.
No column needs to be enabled; Conditions are set via a separate dialog only.
The Condition column — enable it via the column chooser.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a standard Tosca grid customization step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You must first make the Condition column visible via the column chooser before you can drag and drop Instances into it.

optionExplanations.A: XL expressions are values, not the Condition grid column.
optionExplanations.B: RequirementSet is unrelated to adding this column.
optionExplanations.C: The property is another edit location, but the question asks about the grid.
optionExplanations.D: Column Chooser makes Condition available in the Details grid.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After changing a generation condition, what should you do before trial-running the updated generated cases?

options.text: Convert the Template back to a TestCase, then reconvert it.
Check the model, review the instance’s source/manual edits, and regenerate it.
Nothing further is required; Conditions apply immediately without Instantiation.
Delete the TestSheet, then create a new one.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same 2-step pattern used after any Template modification.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The existing generated set must be refreshed deliberately; schema validation alone does not prove successful runtime behavior.

optionExplanations.A: Reverse conversion loses model information and is unnecessary here.
optionExplanations.B: Model checking and deliberate regeneration refresh the concrete set before trial execution.
optionExplanations.C: Existing generated cases do not automatically adopt the edited condition.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting the data source discards useful structure rather than applying the change.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can you quickly tell whether a TestStepFolder, TestStep, or TestStepValue already has a Condition set, without opening each one individually?

options.text: Its condition-based instantiation icon has a dotted outline.
There is no visual indicator; you must open each element to check.
Its font turns bold automatically.
Tosca sends a notification for every Condition set.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a visual, at-a-glance indicator in the tree, not a popup or text change.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The current documentation shows dotted outlines for objects instantiated through conditions.

optionExplanations.A: Dotted outlines identify condition-based instantiation in the documented UI.
optionExplanations.B: There is a documented visual indicator.
optionExplanations.C: Bold usage marks are not the documented condition indicator.
optionExplanations.D: A notification for each condition is not the described mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What distinguishes a Template instantiation Condition from an execution-time IF condition?

options.text: Instantiation Conditions continually inspect live UI state at runtime.
They are exactly the same mechanism with different colors.
Instantiation Conditions select model elements using source data during generation; runtime IF branches during execution.
Instantiation Conditions can only be used on ExecutionLists.

practiceQuiz.hint: Ask when the condition is evaluated and what data it uses.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A generation condition determines the concrete model created; runtime branching is a separate TestCase mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Live-UI evaluation describes runtime behavior, not data-based generation selection.
optionExplanations.B: The evaluation phase and purpose differ, not merely appearance.
optionExplanations.C: Generation conditions choose concrete structure; execution IF chooses the runtime branch.
optionExplanations.D: Supported targets include Templates and their internal model elements.

quickRecap.value: Conditional instantiation chooses generated structure, distinct from execution-time IF.
Template, TemplateInstance and supported internal folders/steps/values can carry conditions.
&& means AND and || means OR; inspect the complete expression and domain.
Check, regenerate deliberately, inspect the subset and trial-run assertions.
